object_description: double gymnasium raised above a base floor on the hilltop, towering over the complex
geometry_property: double gymnasium above a base floor
facades almost 15 m high and largely closed
window bands behind perforated wooden formwork
design_condition: the volume stands as a striking element at the end of the school area on the hilltop in front of the forest edge, its double gymnasium raised above a base floor on the valley side

positive: The new building is deliberately a striking element at the end of the school area
It stands on the hilltop in front of the edge of the forest
It fits into the orthogonal structure of the school complex
The ridge direction corresponds to that of the neighbouring school buildings
The open space connection is made via a staircase and ramp system
The upper entrance leads from the new hard court via an outside staircase to the entrance area
Sports halls and foyer are illuminated via a continuous band of windows on each end
These sit behind perforated wooden formwork
The western corner placement enables integration into the orthogonally oriented complex
negative: The hall building towers over the existing school complex
The forecourts and playground are only peripherally connected to the existing open space structure
The facades up to almost 15 m high are largely closed
Consistent separation of work lessons and sports activities is only possible to a limited extent
Workrooms share the entrance and corridor with the cloakrooms and sanitary rooms
The workroom cloakrooms would have to be relocated and the opposite sports cloakrooms disturb
A direct connection between halls and cloakrooms would be particularly desirable for clubs
The foyer doubles as a long rectangular access area and cannot be closed off
Use independent of sports operations is not possible
The volume spread over three levels has higher air spaces and elaborate spectator stands
The multi-storey structure generates additional traffic areas
Total costs are almost 20 per cent and building volume a good 30 per cent above average
The western corner extends the already expanded construction area by around 4 metres
The distance between the 14 m high south facade and the kindergarten is only around 7.5 m
The hall appears all too dominant overall
The macro-spatial competition with the church cannot be justified for a secular gymnasium
The project is not convincing in site planning, functional and economic aspects
